scenario.context: FitHub is a gym with 3 branches. 35% of booked classes have no-shows, instructors teach half-empty rooms, and wait-listed members cannot get a spot.

hints: Be specific about who is affected and give numbers wherever you can.

content.who: Members who want popular classes and instructors who teach them.
content.problem: Booked spots go unused because members do not show up and the spot cannot be re-released in time.
content.whyNow: Wait-lists are growing and members are starting to cancel.
content.evidence: 35% no-show rate; wait-listed members unable to attend; instructor complaints.
content.impact: Lost class capacity and lower member satisfaction and retention.
content.constraints: No extra instructors; a late cancellation rule must be fair and simple.
content.successMetric: No-show rate from 35% to 15% in 3 months, with attended classes per member up.

reference.whyItWorks: Specific people, a clear problem statement, measurable evidence and a target.
commonMistakes: Stating the solution (add fines) as the problem

scenario.context: At an e-commerce company, support agents spend about 40% of their time searching internal documents. First response time is 9 minutes against a 4 minute target, and CSAT is 71%.

steps.task: Fill in the canvas, making sure you do not jump to a tool.
hints: Define the problem in terms of time and customer impact.
State what you do not yet know.

content.who: Frontline support agents, especially new joiners, and the customers waiting for replies.
content.problem: Agents cannot find the right answer quickly, which slows replies and lowers answer quality.
content.whyNow: Ticket volume is rising ahead of the sale season and CSAT has dropped.
content.evidence: 40% of agent time spent searching; 9 minute first response against 4; CSAT 71%.
content.impact: More agents needed, poor customer experience, and risk to repeat purchases.
content.constraints: Content is spread over several tools; limited team to maintain it; no budget for a new vendor this quarter.
content.unknowns: Which topics cause the most searches and whether answers exist at all.
content.successMetric: Search time from 40% to 20%, first response from 9 to 5 minutes, CSAT from 71% to 78%.

reference.whyItWorks: Defines the problem without prescribing a tool and lists unknowns.
commonMistakes: Writing build a chatbot as the problem

scenario.context: A B2B analytics company hears that onboarding takes too long. Data: average onboarding is 11 weeks. Sales says enterprise customers wait on security reviews, customer success says mid-market customers wait on data setup, and a competitor now promises go-live in 4 weeks. Renewals for the biggest cohort are due next quarter.

steps.task: Choose a focus, justify it, and fill in the canvas.
hints: The statement onboarding is slow is too broad; narrow the who.
Say why you picked this segment over the others.

content.focus: Mid-market customers, because they are the largest group, their delay is within our control (data setup), and enterprise security reviews are largely outside our control.
content.who: Mid-market customer admins and the implementation managers who support them.
content.problem: Customers take too long to connect and validate their data, so they reach first value late.
content.whyNow: The renewal cohort is next quarter and a competitor promises 4 weeks.
content.evidence: 11 week average; customer success reports data setup as the main wait; need a breakdown of weeks per stage to confirm.
content.impact: Renewal risk, delayed expansion and heavy implementation cost.
content.constraints: Limited engineering time, customer data quality varies, security reviews cannot be skipped.
content.successMetric: Time to first value from 11 weeks to 6 for mid-market, with onboarding CSAT up and no rise in setup errors.

reference.whyItWorks: Narrows a vague complaint to one segment with a clear reason and says what must be verified.
commonMistakes: Trying to fix every segment at once
Accepting sales opinions without a stage-by-stage breakdown
